title: Lucinda Patterson:
headline: CASS's Chief Financial Officer tells donors why they matter now and promises their gifts go to clients, nowhere else.
story: Cold open on the stake, in the CFO's own words: government funding is almost gone, so CASS depends on donors. Then who she is, then her order of things: clients come first.

The middle is the reassurance a donor is looking for: their gifts go to clients, they are not used frivolously, <q>I can't stress that enough.</q> She closes warm: the job is fulfilling and makes her a better person.
This is the short vertical cut. The long horizontal version with the questions is its own item (Lucinda Longform).

bite:0.quote: So I wanna make them comfortable, and I find that people work better if they're comfortable with their position.
What led me here is my husband and I transferred from Las Vegas to Ohio. The only position that I liked, that I had applied for, was for a nonprofit.

When I got that position and learned what All In entailed, it was a chance for me to learn something new. I had been working in construction for over 20 years, and I was really ready for something new.
So if we don't make sure, if we don't put them first in all aspects of the operations of a business, we're not gonna be able to meet our mission.
We have a president that's very passionate about his work. He is pushing all of us all the time to find ways to make sure that this works.
Oh, Nathan Smith, our CEO president, he's very passionate. And he is so passionate that you can't help but feel the same way about working for CASS.
